newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Saudi SABIC, Stone & Webster in plant deal.
newsitem.headline: Saudi SABIC, Stone & Webster in plant deal.

text.p: An affiliate of Saudi Arabia's industrial giant Saudi Basic Industries Corp (SABIC) said it had signed an agreement to use technology of the U.S. firm Stone & Webster for a new propane cracking unit.
Arabian Petrochemical Company (Petrokemya) said on Wednesday the deal was signed in Riyadh and "marks the beginning of basic engineering work for the new world-scale ethylene plant".
It gave no value for the deal.
The unit is part of Petrokemya's expansion programme to build a flexible feedstock (propane or ethane) ethylene plant with an annual production capacity of 800,000 tonnes.
Petrokemya is a wholly-owned affiliate of SABIC, which is 70 percent owned by the Saudi government.
A company statement said the deal "covers the basic design package as well as procurement services for 'long lead' (critical) equipment".
The plant, expected to come on stream in the year 2000, will also have the capacity to produce up to 750,000 tonnes a year of propylene.
"Its capacity will be flexible, depending on the feedstock mix used by the cracking unit at any given time," SABIC's vice-chairman Ibrahim bin Salameh said in the statement.
Established in 1981, Petrokemya produces around 2.3 million tonnes of ethylene, propylene, polystyrene, butene-1, butadiene and benzene.
